content_voiceover: This slide outlines a stepwise laboratory approach to working up a coagulation inhibitor. Step one is general screening, where you compare patient plasma mixed one to one with normal plasma against normal plasma alone. If the mixture corrects, you're likely dealing with a pure factor deficiency. If it doesn't correct, you're dealing with an inhibitor. Step two identifies the type of inhibitor by comparing an immediate PTT reading to one after one to two hours of incubation. Inhibitors that prolong the PTT immediately, without needing incubation, include lupus anticoagulant, factor nine inhibitor, and high titer factor eight inhibitor. In contrast, a low titer factor eight inhibitor often shows time dependent prolongation, meaning the PTT only becomes abnormal after that incubation period, because the antibody needs time to neutralize the factor. There's also a further screening trick here, diluting the patient plasma fifty or a hundred fold before mixing, which helps unmask a high titer factor eight inhibitor that might otherwise be missed. Step three addresses low titer inhibitors specifically, using a four to one ratio of patient to normal plasma with two hours of incubation, which increases the antibody's relative concentration and sensitivity of detection.
keypoints: Step one, screening, compares patient plus normal plasma to normal plasma alone
Step two distinguishes immediate versus time-dependent inhibitors
Immediate prolongation suggests lupus anticoagulant, factor nine inhibitor, or high titer factor eight inhibitor
Time-dependent prolongation after incubation suggests factor eight inhibitor
Step three uses a four to one patient to normal ratio to catch low titer inhibitors
keypoint_voiceover: Keep this three step framework in mind. First, screen with a one to one mix to separate deficiency from inhibitor. Second, use immediate versus incubated PTT to characterize the inhibitor, since lupus anticoagulant and high titer factor eight or nine inhibitors act right away, while low titer factor eight inhibitor often needs incubation time to show up. Third, when you suspect a low titer inhibitor specifically, boost sensitivity with a four to one patient to normal plasma mix and two hours of incubation.
